questions.question: What does final mean when it is placed on a class?
questions.explanation: A final class cannot appear after extends. You can still create objects of it, as with String.

questions.question: What is a blank final field?
options: A final field set to null
A final field of type String
A final field with no initial value that every constructor must assign once
A final field that the JVM sets to zero
questions.explanation: The compiler checks that each constructor assigns the blank final exactly once.

questions.question: final List<String> bill = new ArrayList<>(); bill.add("Ink"); bill.add("Pen"); System.out.println(bill.size()); What is printed?
questions.explanation: final fixes the reference only. The list itself is mutable, so both adds succeed.

questions.question: final int pages = 3; pages++; Why does this fail?
options: A final variable cannot be assigned again, and ++ is an assignment
questions.explanation: pages++ means pages = pages + 1, which reassigns a final variable, so the compiler rejects it.

questions.question: class Bill { final int tax() { return 18; } } class Gst extends Bill { int tax() { return 12; } } What is wrong?
options: Gst cannot override tax() because it is final in Bill
questions.explanation: A final method can be inherited and called, but no subclass may override it.

questions.question: final int[] qty = {4, 7}; qty[1] = 10; System.out.println(qty[0] + qty[1]); What is printed?
questions.explanation: The array reference is final, but its elements can change, so 4 + 10 = 14 is printed.

questions.question: String cur = "Rs "; Function<Integer, String> f = a -> cur + a; cur = "USD "; Why does this not compile?
options: Strings cannot be used in lambdas
cur is reassigned, so it is not effectively final and the lambda cannot capture it
questions.explanation: Lambdas capture only final or effectively final locals. Removing the reassignment fixes it.

questions.question: What is the status of the finalize() method in modern Java?
options: It is deprecated since Java 9 and may never run
It runs every time an object goes out of scope
It is required in every class
questions.explanation: finalize is unreliable and was deprecated in Java 9. Use try-with-resources or finally for cleanup.

questions.question: List<String> x = List.of("A"); try { x.add("B"); System.out.println("added"); } catch (UnsupportedOperationException e) { System.out.println("refused"); } What is printed?
questions.explanation: List.of returns an immutable list, so add throws UnsupportedOperationException and the catch prints refused.

questions.question: Which JDK class is declared final?
questions.explanation: String is final so no subclass can change its behaviour. ArrayList, Object and Thread can all be extended.
